the-rating-can-be-cleared-by-a-reader.why: THE GATE ON THE CORRECTION, REMOVED. `insurer.update` is held by OFFICE_ADMINISTRATOR alone, and with the check gone a Compliance Officer — who holds `insurer.read` and nothing that writes — is offered a button that erases this office's own recorded judgement about an insurer's solvency. The SERVER still refuses with a 403, so nothing is destroyed; what breaks is the frontend directive's most explicit rule, that a control a role cannot use does not exist on their screen, and the reader learns it by clicking. `insurers.spec.ts` fails on the test named for a reader without the write codes — and that assertion is ANCHORED on the rating value being on screen, which is what stops it passing against a fixture that simply has no rating to clear.

the-rating-renders-without-its-date.why: THE STATE THIS SCREEN WAS IN UNTIL 2026-10-23, RESTORED: the rating with no date on it. `financialStrengthRatingAsOf` has always been on the wire and the screen's hand-copied interface did not declare it, so the office's own solvency judgement rendered bare — which is the exact defect decision 93 exists to prevent, one layer above the clear control, because a rating attributed to a month that has passed is a judgement nobody made today. **NOTHING COULD SEE IT AND THAT IS THE POINT OF THIS PLANT**: TypeScript cannot check an interface a screen declares by hand over HTTP, the api's view spec pins the field on ITS side and is satisfied, and a Playwright mock supplies whatever the screen reads — so the omission was invisible from every direction until an assertion existed on the rendered text. `insurers.spec.ts` fails on `(as of 2026-03-01)` in the decision-43 test. **AND THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS PLANT DID NOT TEST WHAT IT CLAIMED, which is recorded here rather than quietly fixed.** It replaced the null check with `true ?`, and that broke TypeScript's NARROWING of `insurer` — the build failed with three `TS18047: 'insurer' is possibly 'null'` errors and Playwright never started, so the plant proved nothing about whether any test observes the date. A plant must disable the MECHANISM and leave the structure; this one now truncates the date to zero characters inside the same narrowed branch, which compiles, renders exactly the old bare rating, and kills exactly one assertion. Same lesson as the plant that deleted a JSX block and took eight tests with it.

the-clear-control-survives-having-nothin.why: THE OTHER HALF OF THE SAME CONDITION, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT DEFECT — which is why the two are separate plants rather than one. The has-something-to-clear test is dropped and the PERMISSION gate is kept, so an administrator looking at an insurer with NO rating is offered a Clear button: it answers 200 and does nothing, because the api treats "already clear" as the state the caller asked for. A control that is always available and sometimes inert is how a reader stops believing the screen reflects the record. It also makes the api's own no-op branch reachable from the product, where today it is unreachable by construction — which is what that branch's comment now claims, having been wrong about this screen twice before. `insurers.spec.ts` fails on the decision-43 test's LAST assertion, that the control is gone once there is nothing left to clear, and ONLY on that one: the read-only test still passes, so each half of the condition is independently observed. **CORRECTED FROM THE MEASUREMENT: the first version flipped `&&` to `||`, and that killed TWO tests rather than one** — either disjunct alone renders the control, so the Compliance reader satisfied the second one and the permission absence broke too. A plant that trips two guards cannot say which half of a condition each guard observes, which is the whole reason this condition has two plants.
